value.proof: `just route-inventory-check` (and the route_inventory_tests) pass with the corrected entries; a test fails if a seat-authority entry has no operation class.

Daemon tests: nonce registration issues a token once; a replayed or expired nonce is refused by name; two concurrent registrations with one nonce yield one token and one E-RS-SPAWN-NONCE-USED plus an anomaly; a public-facts registration gets neither token nor context grant (and the old reissue path is gone); rotation keeps the old token valid until the new one is presented; tombstone, supersede and observed-dead revoke; a bounce keeps a live seat's token valid; a fault injected mid-transaction leaves no consumed nonce and no digest.

Daemon tests: a pid outside any seat tree is refused; a bash-tool-shaped child two hops below its harness passes as that seat; the walk stops at the nearest boundary and never validates through a shared tmux server or launchd; spoonbill's H to M to S to P chain (M dies, S is reparented) refuses P; a dead connector's inherited connection is refused on the next request; a uid mismatch and a missing pid refuse; the index cap refuses the 4,097th registration; an adopted seat over the socket gets a token. macOS clippy and tests run locally before push (CI is Linux only).

Daemon tests: two live sessions under one Copilot boundary make a shim-shaped tokenless request refused with the ruled text, while each host's token request passes; after one session's owner dies, tokenless authority returns; a public session id never moves ownership.

Tests: a registration response is the only serialization carrying the token (assert over /health, roster, cards, spine events and the daemon log for a seeded token); a remote-listener request with a token is refused; the socket-failure path is counted as neither.

Client tests (TS proof is CI on the exact head, C25): each long-lived client stores the token only in memory and presents it; the shim and pij-rs connect over the socket. A live canary on the deployed daemon (disposable seats, one per harness pij spawns: Copilot, OMP, Claude) shows each completing a send, an inbox claim and a report with the capability, recorded as receipts.

Daemon tests: a token send, a peer-credential send and an asserted-only send each increment the right counter; the same operation reached through an alias and through HEAD counts in its class; the counters are bounded (no growth with seats or requests).

Daemon tests: an asserted-only send as another seat is refused E-RS-SEAT-CAPABILITY; the #152 pane-replay regression flips; a parent sending as itself to its child still works. Receipts: the /health send-as counter readings (two, a working day apart) showing zero 'neither' under traffic, and each client's proven send.

EXTEND: spawn_sites.rs covers any new launch site; private-daemon spawn deltas per verb with data.pid; live at-rest before and after deploy (`pij-rs --json ping | jq .data.spawns` twice 60 s apart, `just spawn-rate --seconds 20`).
value.note: Per the workshop's cost table. A long-lived token request adds one SHA-256 of 32 bytes, a constant-time compare and a lookup in a warm digest map. A tokenless request adds one peer-credential read per connection, a start re-read per request, and a walk of at most 16 hops (typically 1 to 3), each an in-process parent read, a start read and one hash lookup in the boundary index; no roster scan, no census. Nothing launches per request, so nothing per tick per seat. Bootstrap and rotation run once per incarnation (any C27 `ps` argv check stays here). Lifecycle: one store read of live digests after a bounce; nonces expire with the registration window, no sweep; the boundary index is capped at 4,096 and event-maintained. Measure before and after deploy: ping .data.spawns per call site and just spawn-rate, plus daemon CPU at rest with the fleet live, since every per-tick heartbeat, inbox and activity call now carries the check.
